-- ============================================================================
-- Storage buckets — logically separated per the spec (photos/video/audio/
-- screenshots/originals). All buckets are PRIVATE: the reader never gets a
-- public URL, only short-lived signed URLs generated by our own backend
-- (edge function), which additionally checks the reader password/RLS state
-- before signing. This keeps "no auth needed to read, but also not just an
-- open public bucket anyone can enumerate" — matches the "no registration/
-- password unless I turn it on" requirement while not exposing raw storage.
-- ============================================================================

insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit)
values
  ('photos', 'photos', false, 26214400),        -- 25 MB
  ('videos', 'videos', false, 209715200),        -- 200 MB
  ('audio', 'audio', false, 26214400),           -- 25 MB
  ('stickers', 'stickers', false, 5242880),      -- 5 MB
  ('screenshots', 'screenshots', false, 26214400),
  ('thumbnails', 'thumbnails', false, 5242880),
  ('originals', 'originals', false, 209715200)   -- raw ZIP archives, admin-only, kept for re-processing
on conflict (id) do nothing;

-- Only the admin (owner) may read/write storage objects directly. The reader
-- never talks to Storage directly — it goes through an edge function that
-- issues signed URLs after checking the corresponding `media`/`screenshots`
-- row is published (see supabase/functions/get-media-url).
create policy "admin full access to all buckets"
  on storage.objects for all
  using (is_admin())
  with check (is_admin());
